claims.claim: In Green Lake, Maine (44 bass, summer 1993), large bass (> 406 mm) used water deeper than 8 m in late summer more than small and medium fish, which used cover more
claims.note: The paper already marks it 'abstract only'. The USGS abstract says the same: 44 smallmouth in three size classes radio-tracked 10 June–1 September 1993; large (> 406 mm) used > 8 m more often than small (248–279 mm) or medium (305–356 mm) fish in late summer (15 July–1 September), and middepths (4–8 m) more than small fish; small fish used cover more in early summer, small and medium more than large in late summer; small fish had smaller summer ranges.

claims.claim: Green Lake is the only Maine telemetry found for any of these species
claims.note: Not a claim the source can settle, but a search turned up other Maine telemetry of smallmouth: the same tagged Green Lake fish in Cole & Moring 1997, Fisheries Research 31:269–273 (survey error), and radio-tracked smallmouth in the Rapid River, Maine, 2005 (USGS record 'Summer movements of sub-adult brook trout, landlocked Atlantic salmon, and smallmouth bass in the Rapid River, Maine', J. Freshwater Ecology). Narrow it to 'the only Maine LAKE telemetry found'.

claims.claim: 25–28-cm Maine bass are still shallower than large adults (Ridgway 2002; Cole & Moring 1997)
claims.note: Consistent with the abstract's small class of 248–279 mm, which used deep water less than > 406-mm fish in late summer.
